# TagAction

> A tiny script that makes plain, semantic HTML behave the way people expect: sortable tables, copy buttons on code, show/hide on password fields, dialogs that open from a button, dropdown menus, live totals. No classes, no build step, no page script, no new syntax. Write standard HTML elements and attributes; TagAction finds them. Every page still works with JavaScript off.

Add this to `<head>` (with or without TagBrush.css, which it is designed to sit beside):

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tagaction@0/tagaction.min.js" defer></script>
```

## Rules for writing pages

- Write the HTML you would write anyway. TagAction adds behavior to native elements and ARIA attributes; there is nothing to call and no classes to add.
- Do not write JavaScript for the behaviors below. Do not add `onclick` handlers, IDs for scripts, or framework attributes for them.
- Keep pages usable without JavaScript. A control that only works with TagAction (a filter box with no form, an "Add row" button) may carry `hidden`; TagAction shows it.
- Turn TagAction off for an element and everything inside it with `data-tagaction="off"`.
- Content added later (htmx swaps, page scripts) is enhanced automatically. To enhance content yourself, call `TagAction.init(element)`.

## Automatic behaviors (no attributes needed)

- Dialogs: a modal `<dialog>` closes when you click its backdrop. Add `closedby="closerequest"` to keep it open. Open one from a button with the browser's own attributes: `<button commandfor="confirm" command="show-modal">Delete</button><dialog id="confirm"><form method="dialog"><p>Delete this file?</p><button value="cancel">Cancel</button><button value="ok">Delete</button></form></dialog>`. Close from inside with `command="close"`.
- Tables: every `<table>` with a `<thead>` and two or more body rows sorts when you click a column header, and sets `aria-sort`. Numbers sort as numbers. Put the sort value in `<data value="1200">$1.2k</data>` or `<time datetime="2026-11-06">` when the shown text would sort wrong. `data-tagaction="off"` on a `<th>` keeps that column unsortable. A column of numbers (header included) lines up on the right in even-width figures; an `align` attribute or your own `text-align` wins.
- Forms: validation messages (from `required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`, `minlength`, …) appear as text under the field instead of a bubble, and `aria-invalid` is set. A `<small>` right after the field is used for the message, and its help text comes back once the field is fixed. Where messages go: after the field; after the `<label>` that wraps a checkbox; at the end of the `<fieldset>` around a radio group, so put a required radio group in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`. The submit button is disabled with `aria-busy="true"` while the form is sent. A `method="post"` form with unsent changes warns before you leave the page.
- `<textarea>` without `rows` grows as you type. With `maxlength`, a counter shows how many characters are used: `<textarea maxlength="280"></textarea>`. The counter goes after the field's help `<small>`, if it has one. In a form, Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac) sends it, with validation; keep a submit button.
- `<input type="file" multiple>` lists the chosen file names. Files can be dropped onto any file input or its `<label>`.
- `<input type="password">` gets a Show/Hide button.
- `<pre>` gets a Copy button.
- `<time datetime="2026-11-06T17:00Z">Nov 6, 5 PM UTC</time>`: a time with a timezone is shown in the reader's own timezone and language.
- `<nav>`: the link to the current page gets `aria-current="page"` (unless one is already marked). In a nav whose links all point to sections of the page, the link to the section on screen gets `aria-current="true"` as you scroll.
- `<h2>` and `<h3>` with an `id` get a "#" link to the section.
- Images: a link around an image that points to an image file (a URL ending in `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.webp`, `.avif`, `.gif`, or `.svg`) opens it in a viewer instead of a new page: `<a href="photo-large.jpg"><img src="photo.jpg" alt="Harbor at dusk"></a>`. An image in a `<figure>` shown smaller than its real size opens in the viewer when clicked.
- `<abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>`: tapping it shows the title in brackets, for touch screens.
- `<menu>` and popover menus (`<div popover><nav><ul>…</ul></nav></div>`): arrow keys, Home, and End move between the items. A popover holding links (a phone menu) closes when one is followed.
- Dropdown menu in the top bar: `<li><details><summary>Services</summary><ul><li><a href="/grants">Grants</a></li></ul></details></li>` in the page header's `<nav>` closes on Escape, a click outside, or a chosen link; arrow keys move through it.
- A link to something inside a closed `<details>` opens it: link an FAQ answer with `<a href="#refunds">` and give its `<details>` (or anything in it) that id.

## Behaviors you switch on with HTML

- Accordion, one open at a time: give neighboring `<details>` the same `name`: `<details name="faq"><summary>Question</summary><p>Answer</p></details>`.
- Remember which `<details>` are open across visits: `data-tag-remember` on a `<details>` with an `id`, or on an element containing them: `<section data-tag-remember><details id="setup"><summary>Setup</summary><p>…</p></details></section>`.
- Filter a table or list as you type: `<input type="search" aria-label="Filter orders" aria-controls="orders">` with `<table id="orders">`. Rows (or `<li>`s of a list) that don't contain every typed word are hidden. When nothing matches, a line after the table says "No matches for …"; otherwise it tells screen readers how many rows show.
- Dropdown: `<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="account-menu">Account</button><ul id="account-menu"><li><a href="/profile">Profile</a></li><li><a href="/logout">Sign out</a></li></ul>`. Write the list visible; TagAction hides it until the button is pressed, and in a nav it drops down under the button and stays on screen. Escape and clicking outside close it; arrow keys move through it.
- Relative time: `<time datetime="2026-11-06T17:00Z" data-tag-time="relative">Nov 6, 2026</time>` shows "3 hours ago" and keeps it up to date. The full date is in its `title`.
- Table of contents: `<nav data-tag-toc hidden></nav>` (for example in an `<aside>` beside the `<article>`) is filled with links to the `<h2>` and `<h3>` headings in `<main>` and then shown. Headings without an `id` get one. Write `hidden` so readers without JavaScript don't get an empty menu; TagAction also shows a hidden element around the nav.
- Live result: `<output for="room breakfast">` shows the sum of the numbers in the fields with those ids, or the value of a single field: `<input type="range" id="volume" min="0" max="10"><output for="volume"></output>`. A checkbox or radio counts its value only while checked. `data-tag-calc="product"` multiplies instead, leaving out unchecked checkboxes and radios, so listing every radio of a group multiplies by the chosen one: `<output for="nights standard deluxe" data-tag-calc="product" data-tag-format="USD">`. `data-tag-format` is a currency code (`USD`, `EUR`), `percent` (0.15 shows 15%), or `number`, formatted for the page's `lang`. Write the starting result inside the `<output>` for readers without JavaScript.
- Tabs: `<div role="tablist" aria-label="Install with"><button role="tab" aria-controls="npm" aria-selected="true">npm</button><button role="tab" aria-controls="cdn">CDN</button></div><section id="npm" role="tabpanel">…</section><section id="cdn" role="tabpanel">…</section>`. Without JavaScript every panel shows; TagAction shows the selected one and moves between tabs with the arrow keys, Home, and End.
- Light/dark switch, remembered across visits: `<select data-tag-theme aria-label="Color scheme" hidden><option value="">Auto</option><option value="light">Light</option><option value="dark">Dark</option></select>`, or a toggle, `<button data-tag-theme hidden>Dark mode</button>`. It sets `data-theme` on `<html>`, which TagBrush.css follows. On a page with a switch, load the script in `<head>` without `defer`, so the saved scheme is set before the first paint instead of flashing the other one.
- Copy: `<input id="invite" value="https://example.com/join/4F7Q" readonly aria-label="Invite link"><button commandfor="invite" command="--copy" hidden>Copy</button>` copies a field's value, or the text of any other element. Share: `<section id="pricing"><h2>Pricing</h2><button commandfor="pricing" command="--share" hidden>Share</button></section>` opens the share sheet for that section's link (or an `<a>`'s address), and copies the link where there is no share sheet.
- Matching fields: `<input type="password" id="password"><input type="password" id="confirm" data-tag-match="password">` keeps the second field invalid, with a message, until the two match.
- Search results: a filter box pointing at a list written `hidden` shows the list only while something is typed, with just the matches: `<input type="search" aria-label="Search the docs" aria-controls="pages" hidden><ul id="pages" hidden><li><a href="/install">Install</a></li></ul>`.
- Repeated rows: put a `<template>` where new items should go, and point a button at it with `command="--clone"`: `<ul><li><input aria-label="Guest name" name="guest"></li><template id="guest"><li><input aria-label="Guest name" name="guest"></li></template></ul><button type="button" commandfor="guest" command="--clone" hidden>Add guest</button>`. Ids inside each copy get a number so they stay unique. To make rows removable, give each row (in the template, and any written in the page) an id and a remove button: `<li id="guest-row"><input aria-label="Guest name" name="guest"> <button type="button" commandfor="guest-row" command="--remove" hidden>Remove</button></li>`. The button removes the element it names, and focus moves to the row before it (or the Add button).

## What TagAction does not do

- No fetching or swapping HTML from a server (use htmx, which TagAction works with), no client-side includes, no templating syntax, no reactive state, no components.
- It does not replace native `<details>`, `<dialog>`, or `popover` behavior, and lazy loading is the browser's own `loading="lazy"`.
- It does not style the page. TagBrush.css does that; TagAction only adds small styles for the buttons and text it inserts.
